full_judgment:
18. Contesting defendant No.1 by filing a written statement claimed that plaintiff has/had no possession over the suit land, as such, the suit is not maintainable without seeking the relief of recovery of khas possession and the suit is barred by the proviso of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. 

 22. Thus, dispossession of the plaintiff from a portion of the suit land being admitted, the plaintiff was required by law to seek relief of recovery of khas possession which she did not and, as such, simple suit for declaration without seeking relief for recovery of khas possession is not tenable inasmuch as proviso of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act mandates that no Court shall make any such declaration where the plaintiff, being able to seek further relief than a mere declaration of title, omits to do so and without considering this factual and legal aspect courts below committed an error of law resulting an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. 

 50. Considering the above discussions and the principles enunciated in the referred cases, we are of the view that the plaintiff miserably failed to prove their title over the suit land, as such, they are not entitled to get a preliminary decree in the instant partition suit. Furthermore, the present suit is not maintainable in its present form without a prayer for recovery of khas possession as well as not impugning the Deed Nos.8567, 5078 dated 28-6-1967 and 15-9-1966 respectively. Beside this the plaintiff is also bound by the judgment and decree of Suit No.57 of 1967 passed by the learned Sub-Judge, 1st Court, Chittagong. As such the instant suit is liable to be dismissed.
